name: security-dotnet-data-protection-context-review
intent: ASP.NET Core Data Protection key-ring and purpose isolation
artifacts: Key storage/access, application discriminator, purpose chain, token consumer and deployment slots.
trace: Trace which applications/tenants share keys and purposes and whether one protected payload is accepted in another authorization context.
experiment: Use two local owned apps with synthetic protected tokens; compare intended unprotect and a cross-app/purpose attempt.
disproof: Sharing a key ring can be intentional for a single security boundary; successful decryption is not a privilege grant unless the consumer accepts the payload context.
repair: Separate key access/purposes according to the intended boundary and retest legitimate migration and token use.
branch_decisions: Shared keys and application names can deliberately enable SSO. Compare intended security domains, application discriminator and the full purpose chain, plus key-ring read/write authority. Unprotect success alone is not an authorization grant: verify how the consumer interprets tenant, identity and purpose before asserting that another application can impersonate a protected user.
